html:
Botswana suffered one of the world's worst HIV epidemics from the 1990s, with about a quarter of adults infected at its peak and life expectancy falling sharply.

Good roads, mobility and migrant labour helped the virus spread, and it threatened to undo the gains of diamond wealth. In 2002 Botswana became the first country in Africa to offer free antiretroviral drugs to all who needed them, with help from foreign donors.

Deaths fell and life expectancy recovered. Botswana later became one of the first countries to reach United Nations testing and treatment targets, and it greatly reduced infection of babies at birth. It is a central story of the AIDS epidemic in Africa and of Botswana's state.
sum: Botswana suffered one of the world's worst HIV epidemics from the 1990s, with about a quarter of adults infected at its peak and life expectancy falling sharply.
